introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2021. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION II (30 minutes) - DATA ANALYSIS**

The current, $I$, through a certain electrical device is related to the potential difference, $V$, across its terminals by the equation:

$$I = I_0\, e^{-eV/2\beta T}$$

Where $e$ is the electronic charge, $T$ is the temperature at which the current is flowing and equals $298\ \mathrm{K}$ and $\beta$ is a constant.

The following results were obtained using the device:

| $I / \times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{A}$ | $V / \times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{V}$ |
|---|---|
| 29.2 | 2.9 |
| 25.9 | 3.5 |
| 23.0 | 4.1 |
| 20.8 | 4.6 |
| 19.2 | 5.0 |
| 17.6 | 5.5 |
| 15.7 | 6.0 |
| 14.2 | 6.6 |
| 13.1 | 7.0 |
incertitudes: Question 7 : le sujet n'imprime aucun total ; les marques imprimées (11 + 8 + 1) donnent 20, valeur retenue pour `points` de l'exercice ; `points` des sous-questions = marques imprimées.

Question 7 : l'équation est imprimée I = I0 e^(-eV/2 beta T) ; elle est lue comme I = I0 exp(-eV / (2 beta T)), ce qui est cohérent avec les données (I décroît quand V croît ; ln I en fonction de V est une droite parfaite) et donne beta = 1,37e-23 J/K, la constante de Boltzmann. La phrase « Where, e. is the electronic charge » comporte une faute d'impression (point après e). Charge de l'électron e = 1,60e-19 C non imprimée, posée dans le corrigé.

Question 7 : les en-têtes de colonnes du tableau (« I / x10-2 A », « V / x10-2 V ») sont lus comme « grandeur divisée par 1e-2 A ou 1e-2 V » : 29,2 signifie 0,292 A et 2,9 signifie 0,029 V. Cette lecture donne un beta physiquement cohérent (constante de Boltzmann). Le graphe (a) est à tracer par le candidat ; le corrigé donne la grandeur à porter en ordonnée (ln I), le tableau des valeurs, les échelles et la lecture de la pente et de l'ordonnée à l'origine, sans produire de figure de corrigé.
Question 7(c) : le sujet ne dit pas ce qu'est l'appareil ; la signification de I0 est donnée à partir de l'équation (courant pour V = 0, valeur maximale).

questions.enonce_markdown: Plot a suitable graph from which $\beta$ and $I_0$ can be obtained. *[11 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Choosing the graph.** Take natural logarithms of $I = I_0e^{-eV/2\beta T}$:
$$\ln I = \ln I_0 - \frac{e}{2\beta T}\,V.$$
This has the form $y = mx + c$ with $y = \ln I$ and $x = V$. So plot **$\ln(I/\mathrm{A})$ (vertical axis) against $V/\mathrm{V}$ (horizontal axis)**: a straight line with **gradient $m = -\dfrac{e}{2\beta T}$** and **intercept on the vertical axis $c = \ln I_0$**.

**Table of values.** The columns of the data are $I\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{A}$ and $V\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{V}$, so for example $29.2\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{A} = 0.292\ \mathrm{A}$ and $2.9\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{V} = 0.029\ \mathrm{V}$.

| $V$ / $10^{-2}$ V | 2.9 | 3.5 | 4.1 | 4.6 | 5.0 | 5.5 | 6.0 | 6.6 | 7.0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $I$ / A | 0.292 | 0.259 | 0.230 | 0.208 | 0.192 | 0.176 | 0.157 | 0.142 | 0.131 |
| $\ln(I/\mathrm{A})$ | -1.231 | -1.351 | -1.470 | -1.570 | -1.650 | -1.737 | -1.852 | -1.952 | -2.033 |

**The graph (to be drawn by the candidate).** Axes labelled $V/\mathrm{V}$ (or $V/10^{-2}\ \mathrm{V}$) and $\ln(I/\mathrm{A})$, with the horizontal axis starting at $0$ (for example $0$ to $0.08\ \mathrm{V}$) so that the intercept can be read, and the vertical axis from about $-2.2$ to $0$; scales that use more than half of each axis and are easy to read; the nine points plotted accurately. The points lie very close to a single straight line **sloping downwards**; a best-fit line is drawn through them and **extended back to $V = 0$** to cut the vertical axis.

questions.enonce_markdown: Hence determine the values of $\beta$ and $I_0$. *[8 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Constants (not printed in the paper): electronic charge $e = 1.60\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$; $T = 298\ \mathrm{K}$ (given).

**Gradient.** Use a large triangle on the best-fit line, for example the points $(0.029\ \mathrm{V},\ -1.231)$ and $(0.070\ \mathrm{V},\ -2.033)$:
$$m = \frac{-2.033 - (-1.231)}{0.070 - 0.029} = \frac{-0.802}{0.041} = -19.6\ \mathrm{V^{-1}}.$$

**Value of $\beta$.** Since $m = -\dfrac{e}{2\beta T}$,
$$\beta = \frac{e}{2T\,|m|} = \frac{1.60\times10^{-19}}{2\times298\times19.6} = \frac{1.60\times10^{-19}}{1.168\times10^{4}} = 1.37\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}.$$

**Value of $I_0$.** The intercept on the vertical axis is $\ln I_0$. From the point $(0.029,\ -1.231)$ on the line:
$$\ln I_0 = -1.231 + 19.6\times0.029 = -1.231 + 0.568 = -0.663,$$
$$I_0 = e^{-0.663} = 0.515\ \mathrm{A}\quad(\text{about } 0.51\text{ to }0.52\ \mathrm{A}, \text{ that is } 51\times10^{-2}\ \mathrm{A}).$$

(A least-squares fit of the nine points gives a gradient of $-19.54\ \mathrm{V^{-1}}$ and an intercept of $-0.668$, so $\beta = 1.37\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ and $I_0 = e^{-0.668} = 0.513\ \mathrm{A}$.)

**$\beta \approx 1.4\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ (it is the Boltzmann constant, $1.38\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$) and $I_0 \approx 0.51\ \mathrm{A}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the significance of $I_0$? *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: $I_0$ is the **current through the device when the potential difference across it is zero** ($V = 0$, so $e^{0} = 1$ and $I = I_0$). It is the intercept of the $\ln I$ against $V$ line, and it is the **largest value** that the current takes in this model: the current falls exponentially from $I_0$ as $V$ increases.
